title: Anthropic ships Claude SME with 43 workflows and human-approval defaults
subtitle: The SME tier adds 27 app integrations and forces a human confirmation step on every automated action.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic announced a substantial upgrade to the small- and medium-business tier of Claude on September 15, 2026, adding 43 prebuilt workflows and 27 app integrations spanning CRM, ticketing, calendar, cloud storage, and communications. Every automated workflow defaults to a human-approval model — the assistant does preprocessing or draft generation, then holds for an administrator confirmation before executing. The update lands alongside broader enterprise moves this month, including the Salesforce Claudeforce plugin now heading toward open beta.

The interesting mechanism is not the count of integrations but the default. Rival agent platforms have leaned into 'auto-approve' as a selling point; Anthropic's SME tier ships with the checkpoint flipped the other way, and admins have to opt out of the confirmation step per workflow. That maps to what small-business IT leads have consistently said they want after a year of watching agent-driven data leaks and unintended writes — a real veto point that isn't in a policy document.

It also fits Anthropic's broader posture around agent safety this year, from the September safety-standards talks with OpenAI and Google DeepMind to the tightened refusal behavior in the Claude Mythos 5.1 refresh. Small businesses are the market segment least equipped to run their own eval harness or agent runtime, so shipping constraints in the defaults is closer to a real safety intervention than a governance report.

Takeaway for learners: when you evaluate any AI product for work, read the default settings before the feature list. A tool that ships with human approval on and auto-approve as an admin choice is a different product than one that ships the other way around, even if the surface capability is identical.
